title: Benji and the Seven Days
markdown:
Oh, my dandelions! My darling daisies! Benji the gardener wrung his hands, his brow furrowed like a little wrinkle in a comfy blanket. He usually tucked his tiny seeds in, gentle-gentle-gentle like butterfly wings tickling the dirt! Yes! Because that's what they did! But today, his brain felt like a bird's nest full of buzzy bees! "Which plant needs a drink today? And which one tomorrow?" he fretted. "My peas are practically croaking with thirst, their little leaves all droopy-droopy! But so are my proud petunias, who always stand up so tall and show off their pretty faces! Oh dear, oh dear, which day is it for the giggling geraniums? I just can't remember!" He sighed a big, gusty sigh that ruffled his already tousled hair. Honestly, it sounded like a little puff of wind trying to blow away all his happy thoughts.

And there, on a leaf so green it practically sparkled, sat Dot! A little red ladybug, and guess what? SEVEN shiny black spots! One, two, three... can you count them? SEVEN! Wowza! Dot loved counting things! She saw Benji looking quite perplexed, like a busy bee who’d forgotten where the sweetest nectar was hiding. "Hmm," she chirped, a tiny sound like a little silver bell tinkling. "Why is Benji so flustered? His plants look a little droopy, and he looks like he's lost his favourite digging spade!"

From his super-duper old tree, like a grandpa made of leaves and bark, Old Man Oakle whispered. His voice sounded like a soft breeze whispering secrets through his branches. "Shhh-whoosh-shhh," he rustled. "Benji," he murmured, his voice a gentle rumble, "it's quite a job, looking after so many wonderful plants, isn't it? Each one has its own special thirst, its own special time for a drink. It's like a secret garden schedule!"

Dot, her little legs wiggling with excitement, crawled closer to Benji's shoe. "Days!" she suddenly buzzed, her voice a happy hum. "I know about days! There are seven days! Just like my seven spots! And each day has a name! It’s like a special secret code for the whole week!" She thought of her seven spots, so neat and round. "There's Monday!" she declared with a proud little wiggle. "And Tuesday! And Wednesday! Then comes Thursday, and then Friday, and then the fun weekend days, Saturday and Sunday! Each day is a little bit special, a little bit different!" He'd forgotten the days!

Benji’s eyes, which had been looking so worried, suddenly popped open wide like little blue marbles. "Days? Of course! The days of the week! I know about those days!" He’d forgotten all about them in his busy planting. Silly Benji!

Old Man Oakle chuckled, a warm, creaky sound like dry leaves skittering across the grass. "Dot is quite right, Benji. If we think about the days, we can make a plan. A super-duper watering plan for your thirsty friends!"

Benji’s heart did a happy little leap. "A plan! Yes! A plan is just what I need!" Dot, with a little buzz of encouragement, fluttered down onto a smooth, flat stone near Benji's feet. It was perfect for drawing. "Let's write it down!" she suggested. "So you don't forget!"

Benji, feeling much better, rummaged in his little gardening bag and pulled out a smooth, fallen twig. He began to draw in the soft, dark earth of the stone. He drew seven neat little boxes, side-by-side. "For Monday," he announced, and carefully wrote a big 'M' inside the first box. "For Tuesday," he wrote a 'T' in the next. He drew and wrote for Wednesday (a 'W'), Thursday (a 'Th'), Friday (an 'F'), Saturday (an 'S'), and finally, a 'Su' for Sunday. Seven little boxes, ready for action!

Dot, ever helpful, pointed a tiny leg towards the little pea plants, who were indeed looking quite parched. "Peas on Monday!" she chirped, her seven spots gleaming. Benji smiled, a big, beaming gardener’s smile. "Okay, peas on Monday it is! Hooray for Monday!" Then he looked at his proud petunias, their petals drooping ever so slightly. "Petunias can have their drink on Tuesday," he decided. "Twice as nice, Tuesday!"

And so they continued, Benji drawing and Dot suggesting, carefully assigning each plant its own special watering day. The giggling geraniums, who always seemed to chuckle when they got a drink, were put down for Wednesday. The cheerful chives, who smelled so lovely, were for Thursday. The tall, sunny sunflowers, who always seemed to be smiling at the sky, got their turn on Friday. The bouncy beans, who loved to stretch their stems, were scheduled for Saturday. And the shy little strawberries, hiding under their leaves, were a sweet surprise for Sunday. "Hooray!" cheered Dot, doing a little wiggle-dance on the stone, her seven spots seeming to bounce with joy.

Benji looked at his garden chart, the little earth-boxes on the stone filled with the names of his plants and the special days they'd get a drink. He felt a happy, fluttery feeling deep inside, like a tiny butterfly exploring his tummy. "Thank you, Dot! Thank you, Old Man Oakle!" he said, his voice full of warmth. He grabbed his trusty watering can, filled it with cool, clear water, and skipped over to the pea plants. "Moist on Monday!" he sang as he gave them a lovely, long drink.

The next day, the proud petunias got their turn, their petals perking up as if to say, "Thank you, Benji!" Benji realized that by thinking about the days of the week, he could remember everything his plants needed. It was like a wonderful secret code that made his garden happy and healthy. "It's so much easier when we know the days," he told Dot, who had perched on his shoulder and was busy counting her spots again, just for fun. "And it's even better when we work together! You're the best helper a gardener could ask for!"

Old Man Oakle rustled his leaves, a sound like a gentle applause. "Indeed," he whispered, his voice like the softest breeze. "The days help us organize our tasks, and friendship, like sunshine and water, helps everything bloom. Now, Benji, I wonder what other clever ways we can use these wonderful days of the week to make our garden the happiest, healthiest place ever?"

Benji grinned, his heart as sunny and bright as his sunflowers. "Me too!" he exclaimed, a happy little hum escaping his lips, a sound as sweet as nectar. "Me too! I bet there are lots of wonderful things the days can help us with!" And with that happy thought, he went off to give the petunias their well-deserved drink.
characters: Benji the careful gardener, Dot the ladybird, Mr. Hale
